title: Could you outrun a tsunami from the beach? I simulated it
head: The water reaches the beach.
Can you outrun it?
tag: Full video: how fast would you need to run to escape a tsunami?
description: A 1D simulation of a 2 m tsunami reaching an idealised coast. On land the water front moved at about 30 km/h over the first 500 m. Walker, jogger and hard runner starting at the water's edge are overtaken within about a second; only Usain Bolt's top speed (12.32 m/s) stays ahead. Model, not a forecast. From the full video on Earth Worked Out. #tsunami #science #physics

title: A 100 m head start on a tsunami is not enough
head: 100 m head start.
Still caught.
tag: Full video: how fast would you need to run to escape a tsunami?

thumb.small: the head start is the whole game

description: Same simulated tsunami, but you start 100 m up the beach: a jogger is caught after 17 s, a hard runner after 29 s, a 25 km/h sprinter after about a minute. To stay ahead all the way from the water's edge a walker needs a 13 min 24 s head start. Model, not a forecast. From the full video on Earth Worked Out. #tsunami #science #physics

title: When the sea drains away, a tsunami may be minutes away
head: If the sea drains away,
you may have minutes.
tag: Full video: how fast would you need to run to escape a tsunami?
description: In a trough-first run of my simulation the sea drew back 88 m and stayed out about 6 minutes before flooding the land. The US National Weather Service lists the ocean draining away, a strong or long earthquake, or a loud roar as natural warnings: a tsunami could arrive within minutes, so go to high ground or inland. Source: weather.gov/safety/tsunami-during. From the full video on Earth Worked Out. #tsunami #science #safety
